designation_recoveries.note: Used the explicit Soccol designation as a nominal amount. EPIT's numeric Ti was 1.88 while its comment also said 1.86; the discrepancy was recorded, not silently resolved in EPIT.

1969Boehni.reason: The study varied Re, but Soccol omitted it. EPIT reference 81 also recorded Re as zero throughout, so that entry was not used to resolve the known omission.

2018Shi.reason: The paper reported five Y levels, but the selected Soccol rows lacked a specimen key linking each row to a Y amount. Row order, targets and event outcomes were not used to assign Y.

1994Malik.reason: Known copper-containing grades occurred in this source, but the workbook had no Cu column and the source-specific amounts were not recovered. All source rows were conservatively left pending review; this did not claim that every alloy contained positive Cu.

combined_amount_rule.reason: The source designation gave Nb+Ta together. EPIT split the total equally, but independent evidence for an equal split was not established; the separate amounts remained unknown.

missing_named_element.reason: The designation explicitly named Nb but supplied no amount; a source-specific amount was not recovered.

research_notes.result: Publisher abstract confirmed Re variation; no recoverable row-level composition table was available in the retrieved content.
Methods gave Y levels 0, 0.007, 0.013, 0.019 and 0.049 wt.%. The workbook lacked an unambiguous specimen-to-row link. Bulk amounts were not matched using pitting potentials.
